brief: Colorful, gender-neutral basics for babies and kids. Pieces are $12-30. Parents of kids 0-12 who like bundles and hand-me-down-able clothing.

profile.business_summary: Colorful, gender-neutral basics for babies and kids priced between $12-30, targeting parents of children aged 0-12 who value durability and bundle purchases.
stated_claims: Colorful, gender-neutral basics for babies and kids

relevant_tags.why: The core product is children's clothing.
The brand explicitly sells everyday basics.
Hand-me-down-able clothing implies durability and a sustainable lifecycle.
Baby and kids' apparel is a highly popular gifting category.

persona_conflicts.conflict: disinterested_in 'trendy language, loud aesthetics, influencer positioning' and prefers 'craftsmanship, heritage, quality-focused'
persona_conflicts.evidence: Brand sells 'colorful, gender-neutral basics' at a low-to-mid price tier ($12-30) rather than heritage luxury, which may not appeal to the Affluent Classic buyer.

note_signals.why: Kitchenly's audience consists of family households, which is a direct demographic match for parents of kids 0-12.
Heartfoot has a strong gifting season uplift, which aligns well with giftable kids' basics.
Linden Park features high-AOV, conservative women's apparel, which is a poor match for budget-friendly, colorful kids' basics.

profile.gate_reason: The product, pricing, and target audience are clearly defined, allowing for immediate campaign planning.

config.advertiser_summary: Colorful, gender-neutral basics for babies and kids priced between $12-30, targeting parents of children aged 0-12 who value durability and bundle purchases.

assumptions: Price not given; assumed $25 for a 'budget' product.
Margin not given; assumed 60% (typical for apparel) for the break-even estimate only.
Break-even per customer (guidance, not enforced): $25 x 60% x 1.1 orders = $16.50.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click: verifiable without trusting a pixel. Maximise conversions within the budget: bids move between $0.25 and the $1.80 cap (category default) to spend it well; no CPA target is invented. Guidance: at the assumed margin, a click is worth about $0.33; bidding above that loses money per customer. Set a target CPA or a lower max CPC to enforce it.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: score 0.62, relative fit x1.40; 0.0222 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.26 (cap $1.80)

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: fixed start bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: bid = start x pacing x conversion likelihood, within [floor, cap]: spend the budget on the best opportunities
phases.why: no CPA target was set, so the goal is the most units for the budget

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget, never above the $1.80 cap (category default).
